verifies whether each provided mailbox can be reached through a cheap,
read-only Graph call. When checking multiple mailboxes, pass them together

tools.name: CreateReplyDraft
tools.description:
Create a reply or reply-all draft for an existing Outlook email without sending it.

The draft is threaded to the original message and saved to the Drafts folder,
so it can be reviewed, edited, and sent later. For a reply-all, the original
recipients (excluding the mailbox owner) are populated automatically. Use
cc_add to copy someone in on the draft, including someone who was never on
the thread, and cc_remove to take somebody off the copied line; who the
reply is addressed to is the thread's own and reply_type decides it. This
tool never sends the email.

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the email to create a reply draft for

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body of the reply draft

parameters.name: reply_type
parameters.description: Specify reply to draft a reply to only the sender, or reply_all to draft a reply to all recipients. Defaults to reply.

parameters.name: cc_add
parameters.description: Addresses to copy on the reply draft, in addition to whoever Outlook already copied. On a reply to all recipients Outlook copies the thread's other participants, and they stay copied; this only adds. Each address is copied once, and an address the draft already addresses is left addressed rather than also copied, so nobody receives the reply twice. Defaults to copying nobody new.

parameters.name: cc_remove
parameters.description: Addresses to take off the reply draft's copied line. Anyone Outlook copied and this does not name stays copied; an address that is not on the copied line is ignored. An address the draft addresses cannot be taken off it, since reply_type decides that line, so naming one is refused and no draft is kept. Defaults to removing nobody.

parameters.name: bcc
parameters.description: Addresses to blind-copy on the reply draft. This does not remove an address from To or Cc: it remains visible to other recipients if it is also on either line, including through cc_add. To move someone from Cc to Bcc, include them in cc_remove and bcc, not cc_add; an address on To cannot be hidden through bcc. Outlook never blind-copies anyone on a reply, so this is the whole line rather than a change to one. Defaults to blind-copying nobody.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: How body is read. Plain text reaches the recipient as the characters supplied, line breaks and angle brackets included; html reads body as markup, so tags in it render instead of being shown. A reply draft is always stored as an HTML document because the quoted original is one, so this decides how body is read rather than what is stored. Defaults to plain text.

output.description: The created draft. message_id is the draft's own id, not the id of the message being replied to.

body.value: Thank you for reaching out. I have reviewed the details and will get back to you with a full response by end of day Friday.

List email messages in the user's mailbox.

Returns ordinary mail by default: Deleted Items, Junk Email, Sent Items and
Drafts are left out unless named in folders, folder_ids or conversation_id.

Rows carry a 255-character body preview unless include_body is set, which
returns each message in full up to max_body_characters.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Well-known folders to list mail from. Naming folders replaces the default rather than adding to it, so pass deleteditems to read deleted mail. Combined with conversation_id, this narrows the thread to these folders. Defaults to every folder except Deleted Items, Junk Email, Sent Items and Drafts.

parameters.name: folder_ids
parameters.description: Ids of user-created folders to list mail from. Combined with any value given for folders. Defaults to only what folders selects.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Return only messages in this conversation, across every folder including Sent Items and Deleted Items. Use it to read a whole thread. Naming folders or folder_ids alongside it narrows the thread to those folders, so leave both out to see all of it. Defaults to an empty string, which returns mail from any conversation.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Only include mail whose subject passes this comparison, given as a value plus the operator to compare the subject with. Defaults to any subject.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Only include mail whose sender email address passes this comparison, given as a value plus the operator to compare the address with. Defaults to any sender.

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: Only include read mail when True, or unread mail when False. Defaults to both.

parameters.name: has_attachments
parameters.description: Only include mail carrying attachments when True, or mail without attachments when False. Defaults to both.

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Return only mail at this importance level, and nothing else. Never use it to express an exclusion: setting it to normal to mean 'not low' drops every high-importance message. Use exclude_importance for that. Defaults to every importance level.

parameters.name: exclude_importance
parameters.description: Return mail at every importance level except this one. Leave importance out alongside it: naming both narrows to a single level instead of excluding one. Defaults to excluding no level.

parameters.name: flag_status
parameters.description: Return only mail in this follow-up flag state. Defaults to any flag state.

parameters.name: received_after
parameters.description: Return only mail received on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Defaults to no lower bound, as does an empty value.

parameters.name: received_before
parameters.description: Return only mail received on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). The whole of that day is included. Defaults to no upper bound, as does an empty value.

parameters.name: only_focused
parameters.description: Return only mail the mailbox itself classified as Focused, using Outlook's Focused Inbox split. Sender addresses are not inspected. Mailboxes with Focused Inbox turned off classify everything as focused, so this filters nothing there. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Return each message's full body. Defaults to False, which returns a preview of at most 255 characters per row.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Cap on body characters per row when include_body is True (0-20000); 0 returns the row without a body. Ignored when include_body is False. A row cut at the cap is marked body_truncated. Defaults to 5000.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Property to sort results by. Defaults to received date.

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to descending.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of messages to return. Values above 25 are clamped to 25 and the response reports limit_clamped_to_max; values below 1 are raised to 1. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Position of a further page, copied from a previous response's cursor. Repeat the same listing arguments alongside it: a cursor names a listing rather than a row number, and one handed back beside different arguments is refused. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: One page of the matching messages. cursor is an empty string when this listing will serve no further page, and excluded_folders names what was left out of it.

tools.name: MoveMessages
tools.description:
Move a selection of emails into one folder in the user's own mailbox.

Use this single call for a pile of emails instead of moving them one at a

parameters.description: The emails to act on, as the ids a listing, a search or a message read reported. At most 50 per request, and more than that is refused rather than trimmed. Defaults to selecting emails another way.

parameters.name: conversation_id

What one filing request selected, what it changed, and what it did not.

    truncated: the selection cap is the page. It is empty when count_only was
    set, because nothing was written to report. Each row's message_id is an id
    this mailbox accepts for that message, so a row can be chained straight
    into a read or a further move - with one limit named by id_shape: a legacy
    id, which is what a keyword search reports, stops resolving once the
    message has been filed somewhere else, so chain it before the next move
    rather than after. Every row also carries durable_message_id, which names
    the same message after this move whatever shape the selection was made
    with, and is the id to chain when the move has already happened.

    else and is now in the destination; already_there means it was there
    before this call and is a success rather than a change; skipped means the

    the cap rather than refusing to describe it, and says so in notes; the ids
    it would act on ride selection.message_ids so that refusal can be answered
    by moving them in cap-sized batches.

    conversation id or the search it was given, empty for a list of ids.

tools.name: QueryMessages
tools.description:
Search the user's mailbox with an Outlook KQL query.

Use it when the search needs what named filters cannot express, such as
an OR across different fields or a NOT.

The query is sent to Outlook's search index as written. Outlook does not
reject a malformed query: it may come back empty or return unrelated mail,
so check the results against what was asked.

Junk Email and Deleted Items are left out. Results come newest first, and the index
serves at most 275 results per query, so a walk that runs out of pages has
reached what the index serves rather than the end of the mailbox; narrow the
query, for example with a received range, to reach older mail.

Message ids come from the search index in the legacy REST format; use
conversation_id to correlate results across tools.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Outlook KQL, sent as written. Properties: from:, to:, cc:, participants:, subject:, body:, attachment:, hasAttachment:true|false, isRead:true|false, importance:high|medium|low, category: (name contains), received>=YYYY-MM-DD, received<YYYY-MM-DD. Combine with AND, OR, NOT and parentheses; quote phrases. Example: from:user1@example.com AND hasAttachment:true.

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Return each message's full body. Defaults to False, which returns a preview of at most 255 characters per row.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Cap on body characters per row when include_body is True (0-20000); 0 returns the row without a body. Ignored when include_body is False. A row cut at the cap is marked body_truncated. Defaults to 5000.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. Values above 25 are clamped to 25 and the response reports limit_clamped_to_max; values below 1 are raised to 1. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous response. Pass it with the same query; beside a different query it is refused. A page with no rows and has_more true is not the end: call again with its cursor. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: One page of matches, bodies capped. cursor is empty when no further page exists; query_note is set when Outlook matched nothing on a first page.

tools.name: SearchMessages
tools.description:
Search emails across the user's entire mailbox.

Combines full-text keyword search with structured filters for sender,
read status, attachments, importance, and more. All provided parameters
are combined with AND.

At least one search criterion is required. folder, only_focused,
include_body and limit narrow or page a result set rather than build one,
so they are not enough on their own.

Junk Email and Deleted Items are left out unless `folder` names one of them;
sent mail and drafts stay searchable. Rows carry a 255-character body preview
unless include_body is set.

Results come back in the search index's own order and cannot be re-sorted.

Outlook's search index answers one query with at most 1,000 messages, so a
walk that runs out of pages has reached the end of what the index serves
rather than the end of the mailbox. The folders left out, the Focused
split and the exact category match are applied to those 1,000 after they
are chosen, so a broad term matching a lot of junk can come back with few
rows, or none, while matching mail exists. A narrower term reaches it; a
smaller limit does not.

Use this tool when the user wants to find emails by content, topic, sender,
or a combination of criteria.

.. note::
   Microsoft Graph's ``$search`` on messages is backed by the Microsoft
   Search index, which returns message IDs in the legacy REST-ID format
   even when the client opts into Immutable IDs. Do not directly compare
   these message IDs with Immutable IDs; the formats differ. Use
   ``conversation_id`` to correlate conversations across result sets.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: Words or phrases to search for across email subject, body, and sender fields. All terms must match (AND operator). Defaults to no keyword terms.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Only include emails whose subject contains these words. Matched as words within the subject rather than as the whole line. Defaults to any subject.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Only include emails from these senders, given as email addresses, display names, or aliases. When multiple values are provided, emails from any of the senders are returned (OR operator). Defaults to any sender.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Only include emails addressed To these recipients, given as email addresses or display names. When multiple values are provided, emails to any of the recipients are returned (OR operator). Defaults to any recipient.

parameters.name: attachment_name
parameters.description: Only include emails carrying an attachment with one of these filenames. When multiple values are provided, emails with any of the attachment names are returned (OR operator). Defaults to not filtering by attachment name.

parameters.name: has_attachments
parameters.description: Only include emails with attachments when True, or emails without attachments when False. Defaults to both.

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Only include emails at this importance level. Defaults to every importance level.

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: Only include read emails when True, or unread emails when False. Defaults to both.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Only include emails tagged exactly this category name. Case and surrounding spaces are ignored; a longer name containing it does not match. Defaults to not filtering by category.

parameters.name: received_after
parameters.description: Only include emails received on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates are interpreted in UTC. Defaults to no lower bound, as does an empty value.

parameters.name: received_before
parameters.description: Only include emails received on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates are interpreted in UTC. Defaults to no upper bound, as does an empty value.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Search a single folder instead of the whole mailbox. Naming a folder replaces the default, so pass deleteditems to search deleted mail. Defaults to everywhere except Junk Email and Deleted Items.

parameters.name: only_focused
parameters.description: Return only mail the mailbox itself classified as Focused, using Outlook's Focused Inbox split. Sender addresses are not inspected. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Return each message's full body. Defaults to False, which returns a preview of at most 255 characters per row.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Cap on body characters per row when include_body is True (0-20000); 0 returns the row without a body. Ignored when include_body is False. A row cut at the cap is marked body_truncated. Defaults to 5000.

parameters.name: mentioned_email_address
parameters.description: Only include emails whose body @-mentions the person with this email address (tagged, called out or pinged with @), or 'me' for the signed-in user. Naming the person in text, or listing them as a recipient, is not a mention. Put what the mention is about in keywords. Requires received_after: every email received in that window is read, so keywords then match words as written and attachment_name is not supported. If the user named no start date, ask for one or pick a recent one and tell the user which window was read. Defaults to no mention filter.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. Values above 25 are clamped to 25 and the response reports limit_clamped_to_max; values below 1 are raised to 1. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Position of a further page, copied from a previous response's cursor. Repeat the same search arguments alongside it, only_focused included: a cursor names a search rather than a position in a result set, and one handed back beside different arguments is refused. A page with no rows and has_more true is not the end: call again with its cursor before saying nothing matched. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: One page of matches, bodies capped for skimming. cursor is an empty string when this search will serve no further page, and query echoes the search that produced the page -- a cursor handed back beside different arguments is refused rather than continued.

tools.name: UpdateCategoryName
tools.description:
Rename a category (label or tag) in the user's own Outlook mailbox, keeping it on every
email that carries it, in every folder.

Outlook cannot rename in place, so this creates the new name in the old one's colour, or
uses it if it already exists, joining the emails to that category. It moves the tag on each
email and deletes the old name only once no email carries it. Up to 50 emails per call; a
bigger job is refused before anything changes. A call that stops short leaves both names,
and running it again finishes it. Calendar events and bounce reports keep the old name. A
change of letter case or surrounding spaces alone is not possible.

parameters.description: Change nothing; report what would change and list the email ids, to batch a job over 50. Defaults to False.

tools.name: WhoAmI
tools.description:
Get the signed-in user's profile and the mailbox this toolkit acts on.

Returns the user's name, email, tenant and other profile details, plus the mailbox
the toolkit reads mail from. mailbox_timezone identifies the mailbox's configured
time zone or the fallback identified by mailbox_timezone_source. received_date_time
remains in UTC; received_date_time_local contains its local representation when
available.

mailbox_timezone may be a Windows zone name (<Region> Standard Time) rather than an
IANA identifier. A Windows name covers its region's daylight saving too, even though
it ends in Standard Time.
mailbox_timezone_source says where that zone came from: "mailbox" and "mailbox_utc"
mean the mailbox itself names the zone, whereas "default_not_configured" (the mailbox
names none) and "default_unreadable" (the setting could not be read) mean UTC is a
fallback this toolkit applied, not a zone the mailbox is set to. On either fallback,
do not tell the user their mailbox is configured for that zone.

output.description: The signed-in user's profile, the mailbox this toolkit acts on, and its time zone.

summary:
The Microsoft Outlook Mail toolkit provides Arcade tools for interacting with Outlook mailboxes via Microsoft Graph. It enables LLMs to read, compose, send, organize, and manage mail in both personal and shared/delegated mailboxes.

## Capabilities

- **Reading & searching mail:** Retrieve individual messages (with pagination for long bodies), list messages by folder or conversation, search by keyword or structured filters, run raw KQL queries, list attachment metadata, and check automatic reply settings — all for personal or shared/delegated mailboxes.
- **Composing & sending:** Create and immediately send new messages or replies (reply/reply-all/forward), or save them as drafts for later review and editing, from personal or shared mailbox addresses.
- **Draft management:** Create, revise, and send draft messages (including reply, reply-all, and forward drafts) in personal and shared mailboxes; drafts are threaded to originals and support fine-grained recipient and CC control.
- **Folder & rule organization:** Create mail folders (personal or shared), list folder hierarchies with unread/total counts, move messages in bulk (by ID list, conversation, or search), and manage Inbox rules (create, update, delete, list).
- **Categorization & flagging:** List, create, recolor, rename, and delete categories (labels/tags); apply or remove categories from selections of messages; mark messages read/unread or set/clear follow-up flags — in personal or shared mailboxes.
- **Mailbox settings & identity:** Get the signed-in user's profile and active mailbox timezone, check shared mailbox reachability, and configure out-of-office automatic reply settings (on/off/scheduled, with custom messages).

## OAuth

Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 via the **Microsoft** provider. See the [Arcade Microsoft auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/microsoft) for configuration details.
